title: Causally inferred phase and factorized grasp/seating encoders
coverage_gap: Only LL/HH co-occurrences appear in the ten support episodes. A monolithic policy can use goal_x to predict pickup actions and nut_x to predict late placement. The episodes also expose only a narrow progression of grasp, lift, carry and lower states; a single global latent may entangle these phases with the diagonal layout.
reusable_regularity: Use a goal-independent learned grasp encoder and a distinct ring-to-peg encoder, with a learned four-way causal phase network trained on support-derived coarse motion/contact motifs. Soft phase weights emphasize acquisition/lift or transport/seating, without making any branch disappear. The resulting stage-conditioned features feed one unchanged common DP, not multiple expert controllers. Direct relation and robot/world skips preserve geometric correction signals and permit exceptions to the factorization. No phase clock, planner or hardcoded runtime action is used.
dependencies_preserved: The grasp branch sees hand-to-handle error, ring/handle lever arm, quaternion, aperture and recent motion, but no goal. The seating branch sees goal-to-ring together with hand-to-handle, lever arm, orientation, aperture and motion, so grasp/placement are not treated as independent physical processes.
The phase predictor sees current contact geometry, absolute heights, gripper state/change, hand/handle increments, ring/goal height error and planar distance, never action labels at deployment.
Both branch gates have a .25 floor. Direct grasp, ring-to-goal and lever-arm coordinate skips remain available regardless of phase, preserving peg/clearance information before pickup.

Coarse world hand xyz, raw wxyz orientation, world-axis velocities and goal/ring heights retain robot workspace, gravity, fixed-gripper orientation and peg dependence. Previous native quaternion enters both learned encoders. Only explicitly absent object2 channels are omitted.

evidence_refs.detail: All ten listed episodes are the only training-target source
Separate handle site and ring center; native world action4, fixed end-effector orientation, raw two-observation history and factor coverage
Five LL and five HH episodes; support gripper actions range from 0 to .6, with positive and negative vertical actions
Read obs 0:3, 25:29, 38:43 and actions 26:31: closing aperture near the handle, then action_z=1 at 27:31 and elevated ring shortly afterwards. Ring/handle x offset is about .13 m.
Read obs 59:62 and 86:90: ring near .19 m during transport, then descending near peg xy toward goal height .1 m
Modules initialized only in build_modules; training-only target hook and causal condition/denoise interfaces
The host weights action epsilon loss by 1 with denominator mask.sum()*4 and separately adds training_loss

expected_failure_signature: Falsifiable: factorization should reduce sign-correlated pickup errors in C without having to infer a new pickup strategy from goal_x. Failure may instead cluster at phase boundaries: a missed grasp can be interpreted as lift, or a large E transport error can keep a ring in transport too long. Coarse labels can prematurely predict seating, while direct relation skips might still allow the DP to learn the original co-occurrence shortcut. Phase misclassification and grasp-versus-placement failure counts would distinguish these explanations. No development performance is claimed.

required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42], using metric rather than host-normalized features
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity native world_dx/world_dy/world_dz, .01 m per native unit, and unchanged scalar gripper. Candidate does not clip, add feedback controllers, or change execution horizon.

training_only_targets.name: phase
training_only_targets.shape: [number_of_windows,2] integer labels for the causal historical times max(0,t-1) and t
training_only_targets.source: Exact D_N support obs[k] and actions[k]. No stored labels or cached predictions are consulted at inference.
training_only_targets.definition: Priority order: lift=1 if native az>.6 and ring_z<.18; seating=3 if ring_z>.06 and planar goal-to-ring distance<.04; transport=2 if ring_z>.1; otherwise acquisition=0. These are coarse training annotations, not a runtime finite-state policy or success oracle.
training_only_targets.loss: Negative log probability from the learned causal phase predictor, weight .05. Multiply each of two historical-label losses by mask[:,0], divide by 2*sum(mask[:,0]) with denominator floor 1. This is separate from and does not rescale the common action loss. No loss is assigned to padded future actions.

support_fit_statistics: None; thresholds/scales are fixed physical design choices informed by the inspected D_N and public semantics. No other data, pretrained weights or optimizer updates are used in support fitting.
architecture: One common DP condition_dim=93 action_dim=4. Grasp MLP 26->64->32 and seating MLP 28->64->32 use SiLU. Phase MLP 16->64->4 outputs softmax probabilities. Concatenate weighted 32+32 latents, four probabilities, sixteen robot/world channels and nine direct relative coordinates. All learned modules participate in the joint training loss and are registered in build_modules.
change_summary: Initial scientific design: learned phase-conditioned factorization with an auxiliary support-derived phase loss. This is a separate pre-feedback design, not an A1 revision. Before the first check, corrected the factory/documentation conditioning-width arithmetic from 89 to 93 (32+32+4+16+9); features, modules and losses otherwise unchanged. No feedback-driven edits.
